Your portfolio is already deployment-ready: it’s a static site made from HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, and a PDF. There’s no backend, database, package installation, or build command to operate.

## Realistic options

| Host | Cost for this site | Best quality | Main drawback |
|---|---:|---|---|
| GitHub Pages | Free | Simplest; stays entirely in GitHub | Fewer deployment previews and platform features |
| Cloudflare Pages | Free | Excellent performance, generous limits, easy future expansion | Slightly more initial setup |
| Netlify | Free | Beginner-friendly UI, forms, deploy previews | Free-tier limits and product complexity |
| Vercel | Free for personal use | Excellent previews and future framework support | More than this plain site needs; Hobby is non-commercial |
| VPS/DigitalOcean/AWS | Usually paid | Complete control | You maintain servers, HTTPS, security, and uptime |

### 1. GitHub Pages — easiest starting point

This is completely appropriate for a meaningful professional portfolio, not merely toy sites.

You would:

1. Push the finished site to GitHub.
2. Open repository **Settings → Pages**.
3. Select “Deploy from a branch.”
4. Choose your main branch and the repository root.
5. Receive an address similar to `https://und3fin3d.github.io/portfolio/`.

You can subsequently attach a purchased domain such as `williamgreenfield.dev`; GitHub Pages supports custom root domains, subdomains, and HTTPS. [GitHub Pages custom-domain documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/about-custom-domains-and-github-pages)

One relevant detail: I checked your source and found no root-relative asset paths that would obviously break under `/portfolio/`, so its current structure should suit a GitHub project page.

### 2. Cloudflare Pages — my preferred long-term option

Connect the GitHub repository, tell Cloudflare there is no build command, and use the repository root as the output directory. Every push then deploys automatically, while pull requests can receive preview URLs.

Its free plan currently permits 500 builds per month, 20,000 files, and 100 custom domains—vastly more than this portfolio needs. [Cloudflare Pages limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/)

Cloudflare is particularly attractive if you later want:

- A contact form handled by a small serverless function
- Analytics
- Redirects and custom security headers
- DNS and hosting managed in the same place

Custom root domains require using Cloudflare’s nameservers, while a subdomain can be connected using a CNAME. [Cloudflare custom-domain guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/custom-domains/)

### 3. Netlify

Netlify offers essentially the same Git-connected workflow. It is especially approachable if you later want a contact form without building a traditional backend. It’s a solid choice, but Cloudflare or GitHub Pages would be enough here.

### 4. Vercel

Vercel is excellent, especially for React and Next.js projects. It provides automatic HTTPS and preview deployments for Git pushes. Its free Hobby plan is expressly intended for personal, non-commercial projects. [Vercel Hobby documentation](https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby)

For your current plain static site, Vercel adds little over Cloudflare Pages. It becomes a more natural choice if you later rebuild the portfolio in Next.js.

### 5. A server or major cloud provider

You could rent a VPS or configure AWS S3/CloudFront, but I wouldn’t. You’d gain infrastructure work rather than meaningful portfolio capability.

## My recommendation

Deploy this version on **GitHub Pages now**. It is free, credible, and lets you learn the essential deployment loop:

```text
edit → commit → push → site updates
```

Then buy a custom domain when you’re satisfied with the content. The domain—usually around £8–£25 per year depending on the extension—is likely to be your only expense.

Choose **Cloudflare Pages** instead if you already know you want deployment previews, a contact form, or more room to add backend-like behavior. You do not need to rewrite the site for either platform.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-12 22:07:16Z)**_

Almost:

- Cloudflare Pages gives you a free hosted URL like `your-project.pages.dev`.
- You can connect your own domain, like `williamgreenfield.dev`, for free.
- But you must purchase the domain itself—typically around £8–£25 per year—and renew it annually.
- Hosting, HTTPS, and connecting the domain to Pages can remain free.

So: **free hosting and free Cloudflare URL; custom domain costs only the domain registration fee.**

## My request for Codex:
it says 100 domains in the plan?


---

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-12 22:07:58Z)**_

That means Cloudflare lets you **connect up to 100 domains you already own** to one Pages project on the free plan.

It does **not** give you 100 free domain registrations.

You receive:

- One free Cloudflare address such as `portfolio.pages.dev`
- Capacity to connect up to 100 purchased domains or subdomains
- Free hosting and HTTPS for them

For example, you could connect `williamgreenfield.dev`, `www.williamgreenfield.dev`, and `portfolio.example.com`; you’d still need to own the underlying domains.
